reasoning_traces.think:
Weibull analysis serves as a foundational tool for modeling time-to-failure data in engineering systems. Its dual parameters—shape (β) and scale (η)—capture both the qualitative nature of failure (infant mortality, random, wear-out) and the quantitative timing of failures. The shape parameter β determines whether failure rates increase, decrease, or remain constant over time, offering insight into underlying physical processes. The scale parameter η represents the characteristic life, which is the time at which 63.2% of units are expected to fail. These parameters allow for robust statistical inference even with small datasets—a critical advantage in aerospace and development testing where large samples are often impractical. The method's adaptability extends beyond traditional reliability engineering into fields like warranty analysis and materials science. The handbook emphasizes that while Weibull can be applied broadly, its effectiveness depends on proper data selection and interpretation. Advanced techniques such as Weibayes and Dauser Shift further enhance its utility when dealing with sparse or censored data. This makes it a core primitive for both GSI’s probabilistic forecasting and GSE’s dynamic system modeling.
